reason.correction: Amendment 005 distinguished harness re-execution from provider transport, native validation/repair, schema-mode fallback, and model/provider fallback, but it did not make the distinction a pre-dispatch, meter-owned gate. Pinned Cognee 1.5.3 loopback fault injection established three same-model JSON-object completions for one malformed structured-output root operation (C), and its selected OpenAI-compatible embedding engine established three HTTP attempts before its outer tenacity retry after a local transient fault (B). This amendment supplies a prospective trace and finite dispatch contract for every arm, instead of a product-specific exception.

nativeAttemptTraceContract.appliesTo: every arm, every root operation, every provider request class, and every future non-scored v1.1 run identically

taxonomyResolution.A: A repeated adapter/harness root tuple is refused before the second host invocation.
taxonomyResolution.B: A second meter event at one root/class after a FAILED predecessor is transport retry evidence and is allowed only by the same arm/class policy plus fresh fault-injection evidence.
taxonomyResolution.C: A same-mode meter event after a SUCCEEDED predecessor is native validation/self-correction evidence and is allowed only by the same arm/class policy plus fresh fault-injection evidence.
taxonomyResolution.D: A meter event whose structured-output mode differs from its SUCCEEDED predecessor is schema-mode fallback evidence and is allowed only by the same arm/class policy plus fresh fault-injection evidence.
taxonomyResolution.E: A requested or reported provider model that differs from the locked model is a prohibited model/provider fallback and makes the trace discrepant.

nativeAttemptTraceContract.capDerivation: The selected Cognee embedding path has an observed three-attempt AsyncOpenAI transport cycle. Its pinned tenacity schedule has minimum waits of 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, and 128 seconds under a 128-second stop-after-delay boundary, permitting at most eight outer invocations and therefore at most 24 provider attempts before the meter's independent request, adapter, unit, campaign, and class-budget ceilings also apply. The same fixed cap applies to every arm and request class; it is a stop-loss ceiling, not an expected count or transferable pool.

prospectiveEffect.note: Runs 002 and 003 retain the bytes, classifications, statuses, and findings they actually recorded. They are not rerun, rescored, or submitted as evidence for this prospective trace contract.

countDerivation.rule: Unchanged. The amendment changes neither the arm matrix nor the scenario, seed, repetition, phase, reset, or outer-decision derivation.
